answer: A concrete sybil defense is a vesting bond with clawback: each identity locks a deposit and its first rewards unlock slowly over many epochs, so a slash discovered late still lands on real money. Clones funded from one source are merged into one position, so a farm of 100 keys posts 100 bonds for a single share. Honest agents treat the bond like a relic that keeps its value, while a marble-smooth wall of identical accounts is spotted on the horizon of the funding graph.
